content: De-identified Clinical Note (MIMIC-style synthetic). Patient: 68-year-old male with heart failure (EF 35%), chronic kidney disease stage 3b (eGFR 38), type 2 diabetes, and depression. Current medications: metoprolol succinate 100mg daily, lisinopril 10mg daily, furosemide 40mg daily, spironolactone 25mg daily, metformin 500mg BID, sertraline 100mg daily, aspirin 81mg daily, atorvastatin 20mg daily. Risk assessment: MODERATE risk. Key interactions: Spironolactone + lisinopril: dual RAAS blockade increases hyperkalemia risk, especially with CKD stage 3b. Monitor potassium every 2-4 weeks. Sertraline (SSRI) + aspirin: increased bleeding risk through platelet serotonin depletion. Consider gastroprotection. Metformin with eGFR 38: at lower boundary of acceptable use. Dose should not exceed 1000mg/day. Monitor renal function every 3 months. Metoprolol with sertraline: sertraline moderately inhibits CYP2D6, may increase metoprolol levels. Monitor heart rate and blood pressure.
